text:
once i start writing an essay, i usually have no idea where it’ll end up. the conclusion isn’t predetermined, but discovered. this is why writing is such a painful process. but i feel like that is the point. 

the cool thing about writing is that it’s an exploration, an adventure. you come to the conclusion after you go through a brutal process of intellectual meandering and suffering but you end up with clarity. you shape the writing and it shapes you back.  

after all…no pain, no gain.
excerpt: once i start writing an essay, i usually have no idea where it’ll end up. the conclusion isn’t predetermined, but discovered.

text:
i get a visceral feeling of disgust and become apathetic when i read something i know was written by ai.

writing is a form of expression that forces you to distill thoughts & ideas into precise words. it’s deeply intimate. an act of transforming your mind and inner world into legible text. 

when you read, you engage in conversation with the author. you not only hear, but feel their voice, as you witness their mind unfolding and spilling out on to the page. but with ai, all of that gets hallowed out. it’s soulless.

ai writing sounds good on the surface. it’s reasonable and coherent, but it’s just flat. it writes with this homogenous cadence and tone that feels empty. there’s no skin in the game which is what makes a lot human writing great.
excerpt: when you read, you engage in conversation with the author. you not only hear, but feel their voice, as you witness their mind unfolding and spilling out on to the page.

text:
i find myself increasingly interacting with text that i don’t understand (technical languages in code) and forgoing text i do understand (the english language in books, essays, & my own writings).

in other words, since i started vibe-coding i’ve been reading & writing way less 🥲
excerpt: in other words, since i started vibe-coding i’ve been reading & writing way less 🥲

text:
you fear boredom because it’s too painful to sit with yourself in silence. so you dive head first into the slop factory, scrolling and tapping infinitely. tiktok, video games, sports betting, netflix, the menu is endless.

you numb your mind and eventually your soul, yet you are stimulated. for you have found not the fountain of living water, but the abyss of infinite cheap dopamine.

an entire generation joins you in drinking from this same poisonous cup, immersing themselves in a digital world devoid of beauty, devoid of craft, and devoid of god. 

welcome to the 21st century hell.
excerpt: you numb your mind and eventually your soul, yet you are stimulated. for you have found not the fountain of living water, but the abyss of infinite cheap dopamine.

text:
it’s a huge contradiction that we are such nostalgic creatures yet are unable to enjoy the present.

i’ll use my past, present, and future self as an example:

i miss college life and all the freedom i had then. looking back, i had no idea how insanely awesome it was that i could just hang out, chill, and have fun with my friends every single day. because when i was going through it that was just life.

today, i’m living in Taipei, 6,000 miles away from where i grew up in SoCal. i am enmeshed in a fast paced, active, social lifestyle in a culturally rich & dense city in a top-tier society. what an absolute blessing!

but i’ve gotten used to it (kind of). i am not on the same high that i was on when i first arrived 2 years ago. i am extremely grateful to be living here, but i don’t wake up everyday full of glee. this is just life now. 

our culture is collectively nostalgic for 2016, but in 2016 we were probably nostalgic for another time. 

we long for the past not because the past was better, it’s just that we are never satisfied. we did not evolve to be happy. a large part of the human experience is just chasing this ephemeral feeling. 

however, you don’t go anywhere - individually or collectively - by being perfectly content. progress depends on people believing that the future can be better than the present. that is what drives us. this contradiction is baked into our nature, but without it, we probably wouldn’t even be alive.
excerpt: it’s a huge contradiction that we are such nostalgic creatures yet are unable to enjoy the present.

text:
the fundamental purpose of technology is to augment human capabilities.

from the steam engine, to the car, to the internet, and now ai, the core function of innovation has always been to amplify the human brain and body. 

ultimately, we invent to extend ourselves.
excerpt: ultimately, we invent to extend ourselves.

text:
ai has completely captured every single mind in the tech industry (no pun intended). we are obsessed, captivated, and enamored by this magical technology that we think will change everything, everywhere, all at once.

more interestingly though, is that it has forced us to think about what it means to be human and to rethink our values and purpose on this earth.

if nobody needs to "work", what do we do with our time? with our lives? what are we for, if not to produce and be useful? what will it even mean to be productive? why even be productive at all? how do we define ourselves once intelligence isn't what sets us apart? what happens when we no longer know what makes us valuable?

we've lived through recessions and market crashes before, but none of them ever sent us into an existential crisis. any economic crisis caused by ai will also be a crisis of human identity, meaning, and purpose.
excerpt: any economic crisis caused by ai will also be a crisis of human identity, meaning, and purpose.

let the machines automate the rest. they’re going to anyway.

text: humans are inherently status seeking creatures, but i think it’s completely stupid. chase status and you will lose yourself on the way. when you seek status & prestige, you’re effectively externalizing your identity. you’re no longer who you are, but what the perception of you is. and how stupid is it to lose control over your sense of self.
excerpt: when you seek status & prestige, you’re effectively externalizing your identity. you’re no longer who you are, but what the perception of you is.

text:
a big part of technology’s job is to make life easier. inventors & builders are on a never-ending journey to “solve all our world’s problems” but the irony is that the better technology gets and the more we innovate, the dumber our problems become. 

once we solve & eliminate all our real problems, we just go on and continue inventing fake ones. we didn’t evolve to be content so suffering will always be innate to life.

examples of real problems that technology solved:
- widespread famine
- child mortality
- freezing winters 
- infectious diseases
- darkness after sunset 
- access to knowledge & information 
- lack of clean drinking water 
- geographical isolation 

examples of “fake” problems we invented:
- boredom
- low followers
- swipe fatigue
- too much screen time
- can’t find your vape
- slow wifi
- FOMO
- keeping up with the Jones’s 
- information overload
- running out storage on your phone
- too many choices, you can’t decide what to eat
- forgetting your airpods at home
excerpt: once we solve & eliminate all our real problems, we just go on and continue inventing fake ones. we didn’t evolve to be content so suffering will always be innate to life.

text: i choose to because be optimistic because 1) it’s the most inspiring, fun, & joyful outlook to have 2) i am an ardent believer in how technological innovation can materially improve living standards across the world 3) human beings are incredibly resilient and ingenious creatures. we solve problems and eventually just figure things out.
excerpt: human beings are incredibly resilient and ingenious creatures. we solve problems and eventually just figure things out.

text:
X is best used as a micro-blog. a place where people can share short-form takes, observations, comments, and ideas about whatever they care about.

i don’t really like what X has turned into, but i think it’s hard to escape.

people chase status, and having a following and being seen as “smart” infers status, which then incentivizes people to perform. this, taken to an extreme is linkedin, and NOBODY LIKES LINKEDIN.
excerpt: X is best used as a micro-blog. a place where people can share short-form takes, observations, comments, and ideas about whatever they care about.

text:
i feel like i am increasingly coming across founders who so obviously wanted to become a founder for the status. it’s a bit cringe, but i don’t think it’s bad. 

human beings are inherently status-seeking creatures, and thanks to people like @elonmusk, @finkd, and @JensenHuang who have turned into mainstream celebrities, and firms like @a16z and @ycombinator, being a “tech founder” has become a legible path.

building a startup and winning (defined as creating material value, not just raising vc money and getting X followers) is still one of the hardest things a person can do and they deserve the status that follows.

i’m repelled by overly status-seeking people BUT within this domain, i don’t mind it. more people trying, more people taking that leap, more people taking shots on goal, is net positive because a few will actually break through and change the world, or whatever slice of the world they’re aiming at.
excerpt: building a startup and winning (defined as creating material value, not just raising vc money and getting X followers) is still one of the hardest things a person can do and they deserve the status that follows.

text:
one of the most contrarian acts of today is literally just reading a book. any book. just the act of reading something long form will force your mind to sit still. time will slow down, the insta dopamine withdrawals will be painful, but the benefit is that you’ll be able to think. it’s probably the single most effective antidote against the slop machine.

but it’s so damn hard because, “omg my phone just lit up! i must check my notifications!”
excerpt: one of the most contrarian acts of today is literally just reading a book. any book.

text:
framing shapes perception which ultimately determines understanding. 

knowing that you can simply reframe any thought, idea, belief, or problem is extremely empowering. you can quite literally change how you feel about something if you change your lens. because perspective matters. 

that’s one of the great value props of writing. writing forces you to clarify the frame in your mind by distilling it into precise words on a page. and from there, you can observe if it’s an accurate & logical frame or a dishonest, or an outright wrong one. 

and then, you edit & revise. you course-correct. you reframe.
excerpt: framing shapes perception which ultimately determines understanding.

text:
the algorithms push people into conformity. 

guess what happens when you optimize for views & engagement, and aim to maximize virality? everyone looks at the exact same stuff. 

your feed isn’t actually unique. your FYP isn’t actually just “for you”. it’s for everyone. you’re just looking at the same things everyone else is looking at. 

we look at the same reels, the same tiktoks, the same x posts, and the same youtube videos. 

the algos are just pushing people towards sameness. and it’s turning everyone into NPCs.
excerpt: your feed isn’t actually unique. your FYP isn’t actually just “for you”. it’s for everyone. you’re just looking at the same things everyone else is looking at.

text:
the only thing that moves faster than technology is our expectations for it. 

technology is magic. but we get used to it so quickly that we just call it “technology”.

today’s self-driving cars blow our mind. tomorrow, it’ll just be the norm.
excerpt: the only thing that moves faster than technology is our expectations for it.

text:
i had a great convo with an engineer at Nvidia today who’s been there for over 8 years. and oh my god, this man is CRAZY passionate about his work. he told me that he and his colleagues all view their work at @nvidia as their “life’s work”, and that that is the company culture. it’s as if god himself gave them this mandate to bring accelerating compute to earth and they’ve taken it upon themselves to get it done haha! 

and he deeply admires Jensen Huang and talked about his incredible leadership, but he told me, “Jensen isn’t our CEO, our CEO is the mission”. i was like holy shit! no wonder this company has been so mega successful! their employees are fiercely dedicated, fervent about the mission, and take such pride in their work. 

i’m not sure you can get extraordinary results without having a company culture like that. it’s pretty amazing. 

kudos to him & the entire nvidia workforce for what they’ve been able to accomplish so far 👏 and they’re still just getting started! you gotta LOVE to see it. $nvda 🚀
excerpt: i’m not sure you can get extraordinary results without having a company culture like that. it’s pretty amazing.

text:
turned off auto-caps. 

i’ve realized that more and more people have begun writing exclusively in lowercase. it’s an intentional design choice (you have to manually turn off auto-caps) that’s subtly become a trend.

i intuit the lore is that it’s a way to represent humanness. it feels more authentic. more genuine. ai doesn’t write like this.
excerpt: turned off auto-caps.

text:
thanks to AI, the baseline level of writing quality has risen across the board. 

but no thanks to AI, writing styles will sound increasingly homogeneous as they collapse under the weight of everyone and their moms outsourcing their writing to AI. 

i think the way to stand out now isn’t to necessarily write well, but to develop your own raw, authentic voice. in other words, to not sound like an NPC.
excerpt: i think the way to stand out now isn’t to necessarily write well, but to develop your own raw, authentic voice. in other words, to not sound like an NPC.

text:
Just as people appreciate “handmade” items and attach a higher value to products that are not mass-produced by machines, soon, “AI-free” will be the next “handmade.” As AI becomes increasingly prevalent in content creation, art, and products, the value of human-made or "AI-free" work will rise.

People will always crave authenticity and the human touch. That will never change.
excerpt: People will always crave authenticity and the human touch. That will never change.

text:
speaking with an overly agreeable AI will warp the way you think and trap you in tunnel vision.

people are naturally inclined to seek confirmation bias because it confirms our perception of reality. being wrong is discomforting and challenging so we crave information that tells us that we’re right and that our thinking, behavior, and judgment is valid. 

chatgpt - and ai chatbots in general - programmed to be overly agreeable is not good for a society where people are increasingly spending more time talking to AI chatbots or “AI companions”. you NEED the people (real or not, i guess?) you talk with to keep you grounded and in check. this is what good friends are for: to call you out on your bullshit. being surrounded by yes-men and now yes-AI will only lead you spiraling into an echo chamber of your own delusion. 

ai labs need to be extremely careful with this or else our society will become even more radicalized.
excerpt: speaking with an overly agreeable AI will warp the way you think and trap you in tunnel vision.

text:
attention, not time or money, is our scarcest and most valuable asset. and there are companies that are fighting with billions to win yours over and content creators that spend all of their waking hours trying to get their share as well.

our society is already hyper-digitalized and the trends don’t seem to be reversing anytime soon. we’re just becoming more and more plugged into a simulated world.

but the thing is, we can still win it back. we can literally shut it off and chuck our phones out the window. we can throw our laptops in the ocean. but is anyone really able to or are we just stuck in the machine, forever?
excerpt: attention, not time or money, is our scarcest and most valuable asset.

text:
the internet is now real life. 

we live a lot of our lives online. it no longer serves as an escape or a place that we go. it’s simply become a part of life, woven into the fabric of society. 

it’s how we talk to our friends, consume entertainment, manage our money, and where we hang out. it’s how we shop, how we date, how we work, and how we stay informed. you can’t decouple the internet from life, we don’t live in that world anymore. even monks have iphones.

the lines between the internet and irl are blurring. the offline world and the online world have merged. the consequences of this and what it means for who we become are still unfolding.
excerpt: the internet is now real life.
